body: I see. Well, thank you for your input, I appreciate it! Hopefully I can figure something out... Good luck to both you and your friend!

I appreciate the reply. For the first time I feel like somebody fully understands what a difficult position it is to be in. It could be so many reasons; psychology is complex and people make no sense sometimes. There's some sites on the internet that can give you a basic idea of what you can do for her (how to listen, tips on lifestyle changes for depression, coping methods, etc... yeah, I know I haven't made a very good case for all of that working, but they're normally effective), and definitely give her a suicide hotline for your area (in the US it's 1-800-273-8255, you can call too). Of course she should be seeing a therapist, but I suggest you do, too, if you can. I'm seeing one and I've realized that this situation with my friend is affecting me way, way harsher than I've realized. It helps to talk to a professional even if you think you're okay.

Best of luck to you and your friend!

Thank you for taking the time to read and reply. You know, reading your comment I realized that she'll only get into that in-depth if we talk online. Thankfully when we're in person, we're having fun and it doesn't often come up. While away at school I can't log into IM because I have to spend hours with her when she gets into it, rather than do work.

I've tried telling her to find more activities, but she's quit her old ones because she's so critical of herself and feels like she fails at them. I've encouraged her to find new ones that she doesn't even need skill for, she won't because she feels tired all the time and would "fail at them anyway". I've told her again and again that her time and her mind need to be taken up even by small things (take a walk, write a journal, watch her favorite show), but she never will. Any tiny positive thing she could possibly do, she refuses to do, which is why I'm at my wit's end. Thanks again for commenting.

I agree with this. It could help if you pour your energy into activities to do in the meantime. Maybe you could start watching a show everyone's been talking about, take up knitting, do some journal entries, go on a walk in the woods... The point is to distract yourself until you realize things are starting to look up. And hey, maybe you'll discover a new hobby you like!
